html:
The Viceroyalty of New Spain was the part of the Spanish Empire ruled from Mexico City, from 1535 until Mexican independence in 1821. At its widest it took in Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean islands, Florida and the American Southwest, and across the Pacific the Philippines.

It grew out of conquest. In 1521 Hernán Cortés and his Indigenous allies destroyed the Aztec Triple Alliance, and Mexico City was built on the ruins of Tenochtitlan. In 1535 the crown sent its first viceroy, Antonio de Mendoza, to rule in the king's name.

What made New Spain matter to the world:

  • Silver. Mines at Zacatecas and Guanajuato, and the Mexico City mint, made the Spanish silver dollar a world coin.
  • The Pacific link. From 1565 the Manila galleons carried silver from Acapulco to Asia and brought back silk and porcelain.
  • Collapse and mixing. Epidemics such as the cocoliztli epidemics killed most of the native population. A society of Spaniards, Indigenous peoples, Africans and mixed castes took its place, held together by the Catholic Church.

On its northern edge Spanish rule was weak: the Pueblo Revolt of 1680 drove the Spanish from New Mexico for twelve years. In the 1700s the Bourbon kings tightened control and taxes. In 1810 the priest Miguel Hidalgo began the wars of independence, and in 1821 Mexico broke away.
